task_context.problem_statement: The area of a rectangle is 432 square centimeters. What would the new area be if the length of the rectangle was decreased by $10\%$ and the width of the rectangle was increased by $10\%$? Express your answer to the nearest whole number.
task_context.reference_solution: If the length of the rectangle is decreased by $10\%$, it will be $90\%$ of what it was. If the width is increased by $10\%$, it will be $110\%$ of what it was. The area will be $0.9 \times 1.1 = 0.99 = 99\%$ of what it was. Thus, $99\%$ of 432 is $0.99 \times 432 = 427.68$ or about $\boxed{428\text{ square centimeters}}$.

You're right about the length being $90\%$. Since you're in a rush, the fastest way to get to the answer is to find the multiplier for the width as well. If the width increases by $10\%$, what decimal multiplier would you use to represent the new width?

$0.9 \times 1.1$ is $0.99$. So the area is $99\%$ of the original? I'm almost there, just tell me the final rounded number now.

You've nailed the hardest part of the logic! You know the new area is $99\%$ of the original 432 square centimeters. Now, just perform that final multiplication and round to the nearest whole number to finish the problem.
